body: This was a string before, please confirm that is indeed one of CurrentRefinementsConnectorParamsRefinementType strings.
Previously we also exported a normalised type, I decided to remove it to make things simple.
Previously we also exported a normalised type, I decided to remove it to make things simple.

Will users have to cast the type as [we're doing in the tests](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/453eed3d98f3ba3d8ffa345ad3b50bffb4cb0d1a/src/components/CurrentRefinements/__tests__/CurrentRefinements-test.tsx#L324)?

We use it internally to [create the React key](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/56fcb8ccb185ce24d63ca8f5c8e5ae193836226b/src/components/CurrentRefinements/CurrentRefinements.tsx#L43). That's useful in a multi-index context—so I think we can make it public.
You can pass `items.reduce<CurrentRefinementsConnectorParamsItem[]>` to have it fully typed below (in `filter` and `refine`).
It'd make more sense if this lived in the component file instead (`CurrentRefinements.tsx`).

Well, yes.

At least on the experimental yes, because we are not exporting every single type yet.

It seems that the users have to do some casting at some point or they will get in that case: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/37978528/typescript-type-string-is-not-assignable-to-type since 

If we do not want to weaken the type, the simplest way for them to cast it is to use the `const` assertion ( https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-3-4-rc/ ), this way they do not need to type to be exposed.

Are you sure this is correct? `refinement.value` should be a `number` for a `numeric` refinement, no?

Did you mean `String(refinement.value)`?
